title: Shadow scoring: add shadow output adapter + rubric runner with rubric version pinning
author: Olivia Grant
description:
Context: Shadow traffic duplicates a sample of prod requests to candidate variants and scores the outputs asynchronously. This PR adds a thin adapter layer in eval-harness to consume the shadow output payload shape (control vs shadow, plus minimal request metadata) and run the same eval-harness rubric templates we use for prompt-set evaluations, with explicit rubric version pinning so results are comparable over time and across runs.

What’s included: (1) ShadowOutputAdapter that normalizes shadow artifacts into eval-harness JobSpec inputs (request text + response text + optional structured fields like tool_calls / json_output) without requiring the full original request object; (2) RubricRunner that loads templates by rubric_id + rubric_version, executes the configured metric bundle (heuristics + model-graded prompts), and emits a single ScoredShadowResult with per-metric scores plus an overall bundle summary; (3) Rubric version pinning semantics: the caller must provide rubric_version, and the runner will fail-fast if the version is unknown unless allow_fallback=true (used only for local dev); (4) Test fixtures for representative shadow artifacts including: streaming partial capture (truncated output), tool-calling payloads, and “redacted prompt” variants; (5) Golden tests that assert scoring output structure is stable (field names, types, required keys) so Console ingestion doesn’t break.

Design notes: The adapter intentionally does not depend on Redwood telemetry schemas; it only expects the minimal shadow scoring envelope produced by the shadow pipeline worker. This keeps eval-harness reusable for offline replay and reduces churn when telemetry evolves. Rubric templates are versioned via the existing template registry; this PR adds explicit version resolution and a clear error message with suggestions when a requested version is missing.

Rollout plan: This is intended to be consumed by the shadow scoring worker (ENG-5405) in Redwood. The worker will pin rubric_version per experiment at creation time and pass it through with each scoring job. We can add a follow-up PR to document recommended pinning behavior for long-running experiments.

Testing: unit tests for adapter normalization; integration-style tests that run a small rubric bundle against fixtures; lint/typecheck. CI runs both CPU-only heuristic metrics and a mocked model-graded scorer (no network).

Notes for reviewers: Please focus on the rubric version behavior, schema stability for ScoredShadowResult, and fixture coverage for streaming/tool-calling edge cases.

notable_diff_snippets: New schema (excerpt): ScoredShadowResult includes required keys: experiment_id, request_fingerprint, control_variant_id, shadow_variant_id, rubric_id, rubric_version, metrics[], summary{pass_rate, mean_score}, timestamps.
Rubric pinning (excerpt): resolve_rubric(rubric_id, rubric_version) -> Template; raises UnknownRubricVersion with available_versions listed; optional allow_fallback chooses latest semver if enabled.
review_conversation:
Jonas Weber: Can we guarantee the output schema is stable enough for Console ingestion? In particular, metrics[] ordering and presence of a top-level summary. Olivia Grant (author): Yes—added golden tests asserting stable keys and deterministic metric ordering (sorted by metric_id). Also added summary with pass_rate + mean_score computed over numeric metrics only; non-numeric metrics are excluded and recorded in metrics[].meta. Karthik Iyer: For model-graded rubrics, do we store the grader prompt version too? Otherwise comparisons get messy. Olivia: The resolved template includes grader_prompt_version and it’s emitted in metrics[].meta for model-graded metrics. We’re not making it top-level because not all metrics have it, but it’s present for any grader-driven metric. Selene Huang: Re: rubric_version pinning—should we ever fallback automatically? I’d prefer hard fail to avoid silent drift. Olivia: Agree. Default behavior is hard fail; allow_fallback is only wired for local runs and is not used by the shadow worker. I also added a log warning when allow_fallback is enabled. Sana Farid: The summary’s mean_score could be misleading if different rubrics have different scoring ranges. Maybe keep it but make it explicit. Olivia: Updated summary fields to include score_scale per metric in metrics[].meta and renamed mean_score -> mean_normalized_score, where normalization uses each metric’s declared [min,max] when available; otherwise metric is excluded from mean. Nadia Rahman: Fixture naming—can we include one that simulates the partial-capture case we saw in SUP-28477? Olivia: Added fixture shadow_streaming_partial_truncated.json and asserts that truncated=true propagates into metrics[].meta so downstream can filter.

Requested changes: (1) Make resolve_rubric error include available_versions; (2) Document allow_fallback as dev-only; (3) Add fixture for tool-calls; (4) Ensure deterministic metric ordering. All addressed in latest push.

Approvals: Jonas Weber approved. Karthik Iyer approved. Selene Huang approved. Sana Farid approved (with note to keep summary fields conservative).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Jonas Weber.
release_notes: Adds eval-harness support for scoring shadow traffic outputs via rubric templates, including strict rubric version pinning and fixtures for streaming/tool-calling cases.
